Ravindra Jadeja to Sonal Dinusha, THATS OUT!! Lbw!!

Ravindra Jadeja to Sonal Dinusha, out Lbw!! This is a great phase for India. Looked like they had to wait for the new ball again to strike. Even Prabath was looking comfortable and suddenly they have two wickets in the space of 3 balls. The centurion, after doing so well, misses a simple flighted delivery that spun a tad extra to beat the bat. He cannot believe his own eyes and ball-tracker shows three reds, with the ball smashing the middle of middle stump. Jadeja darts this ball and gets it to spin sharply, Dinusha was on the back foot for an easy flick. Somehow he missed the ball and impact was right in front of middle. Jaddu is bowling from round the wicket so the moment it pitched around off and turned to finish on middle he was a goner. Dinusha is still shaking his head as he heads to the dressing room. Looks like he felt he hit it but UltraEdge stayed silent. Sonal Dinusha lbw b Ravindra Jadeja 100(168) [4s-4 6s-2]

Manav Suthar to Lahiru Kumara, out Stumped!! Ran down the pitch too early. Manav dropped it shorter and wider to push it out of Kumara's reach. Kumara didn't hold back. Wanted a big piece of it over long-off and ended up missing it. Pant collected, took his own time and checked the bails off to close out Sri Lanka's innings. Lahiru Kumara st Rishabh Pant b Manav Suthar 10(5) [4s-1 6s-1]

16:55 Local Time, 11:25 GMT: India will be slightly disappointed to let Sri Lanka get to 284 from 59/4 but 178 is still a healthy lead. Dickwella and Dinusha were involved a determined 146-run stand that not only frustrated the Indians but also ensured they crossed the follow-on deficit. Manav and Kuldeep got three of the top 4 after Siraj opened the account second ball of the innings. Dickwella rode his luck and played a breezy knock, while Dinusha showed outstanding composure to play a very mature knock. Jadeja picked up late wickets and the two left-arm orthodox bowlers shared 7 wickets between them. By the way, there are angry dark clouds in the background and the groundsmen are covering the pitch just to be safe.

09:00 Local Time, 03:30 GMT: Good morning and welcome, everyone! We are into Day 4 of the first Test between Sri Lanka and India, and despite rain interrupting play on each of the first three days, we still have a decent amount of time left to force a result over the next two days, provided the rain gods show us some mercy and allow enough cricket to be played. We got 73 overs on Day 1, just 43 on Day 2 and 80.2 on Day 3. That leaves us with two full days and two innings still to go, so there is certainly enough time for the game to reach a conclusion if the rain stays away.
